subject: A better body-fat measure undercuts the childhood 'fat rebound' theory
script: From Agewell Brief: A better body-fat measure undercuts the childhood 'fat rebound' theory. A more accurate measure shows body fat doesn't rebound in kids; BMI rise may be muscle growth. Study challenges 42-year-old theory of childhood fat rebound. BMI rises around age 6, but body fat doesn't. Increase likely from muscle and lean tissue growth. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
